name: Regression discontinuity designs using covariates
query: Did the Head Start program help reduce the child mortality rates?
dataset_description:
In 1965, the U.S. government launched the Head Start program to provide financial assistance to poor families. One of its primary goals was to reduce child mortality by expanding access to essential health services. To determine eligibility for Head Start funds, county-level poverty rates were calculated using data from the 1960 census. Counties with a poverty rate greater than 59.1984 were deemed eligible to apply for grants.

Data variables:
povrate60: Poverty rate constructed using data from the 1960 census
mort_age59_related_postHS: Mortality rate based on data after the rollout of the Head Start program
census1960_pop: Population based on the 1960 census
census1960_pctsch1417: Percentage of 14-17 year olds enrolled in school
census1960_pctsch534: Percentage of 5-34 year olds with formal education in schools
census1960_pctsch25plus: Percentage of people older than 25 with formal education in schools
census1960_pop1417: Number of individuals aged 14-17
census1960_pop534: Number of individuals aged 5-34
census1960_pop25plus: Number of individuals older than 25
census1960_pcturban: Percentage of individuals living in urban areas of the county

name: The influence of waiting times and sociopolitical variables on public trust in healthcare: A cross-sectional study of the NHS in England
query: How does the local proportion of GP‑to‑specialist cancer referrals that breach the two‑week wait standard affect individuals' reported trust in the NHS on a 1–7 scale?
dataset_description:
This dataset contains individual-level survey responses from adults in England merged with local NHS performance measures on emergency and cancer referral waits covering July 2022 to July 2023. Each row corresponds to a respondent observation with institutional trust ratings, demographics, constituency-level context, and area-level waiting-time indicators linked via postcode outcodes to NHS Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) and ICB sub-units.
Variable descriptions:
id: Anonymous respondent identifier that uniquely indexes each survey record within the merged file
trustGov: Self-reported trust in ""the Government in Westminster"" on a 1-7 scale where 1 = Not at all and 7 = Completely
trustPM: Self-reported trust in the Prime Minister on the same 1-7 scale
trustParl: Self-reported trust in the UK Parliament on the 1-7 scale
trustMP: Self-reported trust in the respondent's local Member of Parliament on the 1-7 scale
trustNHS: Self-reported trust in the National Health Service on the 1-7 scale
trustPolice: Self-reported trust in the police on the 1-7 scale
trustCourts: Self-reported trust in the courts on the 1-7 scale
trustTradNews: Self-reported trust in news from traditional media on the 1-7 scale
trustSocNews: Self-reported trust in news shared on social media on the 1-7 scale
income: Personal annual income category with 14 brackets (under 5,000; 5,000-9,999; ...; 100,000+)
emergencyDelay: Proportion of patients waiting more than 4 hours from decision to admit to admission across all A&E types in the respondent's ICB
cancerDelay: Proportion of GP-to-specialist cancer referrals breaching the two-week wait standard in the respondent's ICB sub-unit over July 2022-June 2023
ethnicity: Indicator for membership in an ethnic minority group, derived from survey responses/profile variables
london: Indicator for residence in the London region as defined in the nine-region classification used in the survey
conVote19: Indicator for whether the respondent reported voting Conservative in the 2019 UK General Election
women: Indicator for respondent's sex coded as female based on survey demographics
higherEd: Indicator for completion of higher education as reported in the survey
region: Categorical variable for the nine regions of England used to locate respondents
conShare: Conservative Party vote share (%) in the respondent's parliamentary constituency at the 2019 General Election
unemploymentRate: Constituency-level unemployment rate (%) matched to each respondent's parliamentary constituency
age: Respondent age in years (real-valued), spanning 18-98 across waves
W8: Respondent-level survey weight provided by the survey vendor for national representativeness across pooled monthly waves

name: Europeanisation beyond the EU: Tobacco advertisement restrictions in Swiss cantons
query: How does support for European integration affect the probability that a canton adopts a tobacco advertisement restriction this year?
dataset_description:
Swiss canton-year panel covering 1998-2010, tracking when each canton introduced a tobacco advertising restriction. Each row is a canton-year observed up to the year of adoption, with measures of EU-related public support, opinion on tobacco ads, neighboring adoptions, language composition, population, and party shares in government.

Variables:
year: Calendar year 1998-2010 for each canton-year record
canton: Canton identifier for the 26 Swiss cantons included in the panel
introad: Indicator equal to 1 in the year a canton's tobacco advertising restriction entered into force and 0 otherwise
euvote: Share voting in favor in popular votes on Switzerland-EU relations
puop: Public opinion proxy on tobacco advertising restrictions based on the 1992 national referendum result on banning tobacco and alcohol advertising
neighbourban: Count of neighboring jurisdictions with bans, including contiguous cantons and adjacent EU countries that had restricted tobacco advertising by that year
spatlag_n: Domestic spatial-lag variable built from the cantonal adjacency matrix
timegdk_98: Years a canton's health minister served on the board of the Conference of Cantonal Directors of Public Health (CDP/GDK) by that year
t1: Time trend measuring elapsed years since the start of the observation window
t1_2: Square of t1 divided by 10
t1_3: Cube of t1 divided by 100
tab: Indicator for tobacco economic presence, equal to 1 if the canton hosts a multinational tobacco plant and/or has tobacco cultivation
regcul: Index of regulatory density in other civil-life domains (e.g., schooling, church taxes, alcohol)
gerpop: Share of residents who are German-speaking in the canton population
pop2: Overall canton population size
leftregperc: Share of cabinet seats held by left parties (Social Democrats and Greens) in the cantonal government
svpregperc: Share of cabinet seats held by the Swiss People's Party (SVP) in the cantonal government
cvpregperc: Share of cabinet seats held by the Christian Democrats (CVP) in the cantonal government
fdpregperc: Share of cabinet seats held by the Liberals (FDP) in the cantonal government

name: Does right to work imperil the right to health? The effect of labour unions on workplace fatalities
query: How does the percentage of unionised workers in a state effect the state's occupational fatality rate per 100,000 workers?
dataset_description:
This dataset consists of U.S. state-year panel covering 50 states from 1992-2016, combining annual counts of occupational fatalities, employed population, unionization rates, sectoral employment composition, and statutory right-to-work status; each row is a state-year observation with a derived fatality rate per 100,000 workers and its natural logarithm. The fatalities series comes from the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries, employment from BLS state employment data, unionization from the Union Membership and Coverage Database, and sectoral composition from BLS industry employment, yielding 1,250 total observations.

Variables:
state: State identifier (name or postal abbreviation) for each observation
year: Calendar year of the observation, ranging from 1992 to 2016
policy: Annual index of state policy liberalism capturing a state's overall regulatory orientation (higher values indicate more liberal policy environments)
fatalities: Number of occupational fatalities in the state during the year from CFOI (count of deaths)
employment: Employed population used to scale fatality counts to rates (number of workers or full-time equivalent workers)
rate: Occupational fatality rate per 100,000 workers, computed as fatalities divided by employment and multiplied by 100,000
union: Unionization rate (share of workers who are union members or covered by a union contract) expressed in percentage points
trtraut: Number of workers employed in trade, transportation, and utilities in the state-year (industry employment count)
pctttu: Share of workers employed in trade, transportation, and utilities (percent of total employment)
mlc: Number of workers employed in mining, logging, and construction in the state-year (industry employment count)
pctmlc: Share of workers employed in mining, logging, and construction (percent of total employment)
manuf: Number of workers employed in manufacturing in the state-year (industry employment count)
pctmanufacturing: Share of workers employed in manufacturing (percent of total employment)
ST: State code used for grouping and identification in the dataset (numeric or categorical state code aligned with state)
RTW: Indicator for whether a right-to-work law is in effect in that state-year (1 = RTW in force, 0 = otherwise)
lr: Natural logarithm of the fatality rate variable to stabilize scale and interpret changes in proportional terms

name: The effect of property assessment reductions on tax delinquency and tax foreclosure
query: How does a $1,000 increase in last year's property tax bill affect the probability that a residential parcel is tax‑delinquent this year?
dataset_description:
This dataset consists of parcel‑year panel of Detroit residential properties from 2011–2019, combining assessor records, annual tax bills and delinquency amounts, millage rates, parcel characteristics, neighborhood identifiers, and validated sales information; each row is a parcel–year observation after filtering out zero tax bills and extreme tax‑bill changes to yield 1,612,270 residential parcel‑years under two acres.

Variables:
parcelnumber: Assessor parcel identifier used to link annual tax, assessment, and sales records across years and datasets.
tax_year: Fiscal year associated with the parcel’s property tax record, used to construct annual panels and time indicators.
tax_due: Current‑year delinquent amount owed for the parcel as recorded by the City of Detroit’s annual delinquency file (dollars).
tax_due_lag1: Prior‑year delinquent amount owed, aligned to the parcel’s previous tax_year record (dollars).
total_mills: Total statutory millage rate applied to the parcel that determines liability per $1,000 of taxable value.
id: Internal analysis identifier for parcel–year observations to facilitate merging and indexing within the constructed panel.
curclass: Current assessor property class code (e.g., residential, commercial, industrial) used to identify residential improved parcels.
totalacres: Parcel land area in acres from assessor records.
cioccupancy: Occupancy status code from city records indicating use/occupancy characteristics relevant for parcel profiling.
pre: Principal Residence Exemption indicator equal to 1 for owner‑occupied “homestead” parcels and 0 otherwise.
SEV: State Equalized Value, approximately 50 percent of market value and used alongside TV in assessment reporting (dollars).
TV: Taxable Value subject to statutory growth caps and reset upon sale; multiplied by millage to compute tax bills (dollars).
tract: Census tract identifier mapped to parcels for geographic referencing and neighborhood linkage.
nhoodnum: Neighborhood numeric code per City of Detroit definitions used in mapping and summaries.
nhood: Neighborhood name per City of Detroit definitions used in mapping and summaries.
sale_price: Parcel’s arms‑length sale price after cleaning (valid sales identified via terms and winsorization of extremes) (dollars).
sale_terms: Terms‑of‑sale code used to classify and retain valid arms‑length transactions in the sales subset.
tax_bill: Annual property tax bill for the parcel calculated as TV times total millage per $1,000 (dollars; stored as dollars or $1,000s).
tax_bill_diff: Year‑over‑year change in the parcel’s tax_bill measured in dollars (current minus prior year).
tax_bill_l1: Prior‑year tax_bill aligned to the parcel’s current observation (dollars).
tbill_ratio_lag0: Ratio of current‑year tax_bill to prior‑year tax_bill constructed from annual bills (unitless).
tbill_ratio_lag1: Ratio of prior‑year tax_bill to the bill two years prior constructed from annual bills (unitles).
dtbill_lag0: Percent change in tax_bill from prior year to current year, derived from annual bills (percent).
dtbill_lag1: Prior‑year percent change in tax_bill, derived from lagged annual bills (percent).
tbill_l1_1000: Prior‑year tax bill expressed in thousands of dollars for scaling in analyses (dollars per $1,000).
tb_neg: Indicator equal to 1 if the parcel experienced a negative change in tax_bill in the current year and 0 otherwise.
apartment_2015: Flag identifying parcels classified as apartment/multifamily in the 2015 assessor snapshot for property‑type stratification.
dep_dummy_100: Indicator equal to 1 if current‑year back taxes owed exceed $100 and 0 otherwise (constructed from annual delinquency amounts).
dep_dummy_200: Indicator equal to 1 if current‑year back taxes owed exceed $200 and 0 otherwise (primary delinquency threshold in the main data).
dep_dummy_300: Indicator equal to 1 if current‑year back taxes owed exceed $300 and 0 otherwise.
dep_dummy_400: Indicator equal to 1 if current‑year back taxes owed exceed $400 and 0 otherwise.

name: The impact of recentralization on public services: A difference-in-differences analysis of the abolition of elected councils in Vietnam
query: What is the effect of the 2009 recentralization on whether a commune has public transport?
dataset_description:
This dataset is a commune–year panel for rural Vietnam built from the 2006, 2008, and 2010 Vietnam Household Living Standards Survey (VHLSS) commune questionnaires and merged with district– and province–level identifiers for the District People’s Council (DPC) abolition pilot. Each observation corresponds to a rural commune in a given survey year, with variables describing geography, survey timing, infrastructure, public services, agriculture, nonfarm activity, migration, credit access, health and education facilities, land use, sectoral structure, and treatment status in the recentralization experiment.

Variables:
tinh: Province code identifying the province in which the commune is located, used to link communes to provincial characteristics and the treatment assignment strata.
huyen: District code indicating the district (second‑tier unit) in which the commune resides, which is the level at which District People’s Councils were abolished in treated areas.
xa: Commune code identifying the basic local administrative unit observed in the VHLSS commune survey.
madt: Survey or commune identifier from the VHLSS used to uniquely index communes within survey waves and to merge across questionnaire modules.
ngaydt / thangdt: Day and month of the commune interview date, recording when the VHLSS commune questionnaire was administered in the field.
ngayct / thangct: Day and month of completion for the commune questionnaire or related verification, capturing timing of finalization of commune‑level data.
m1c1–m1c10, m1c11a–m1c11c, m1c12a–m1c12c, m1c13–m1c15: Original VHLSS module‑1 commune checklist items capturing basic commune characteristics and public services (e.g., infrastructure, social programs, local projects), coded as binary indicators or shares and later combined into sector‑specific indices (infrastructure, agricultural services, health, education, communications, household business support).
m3c1–m3c5, m3c2, m3c2a1–m3c2a3, m3c3, m3c4a–m3c4c, m3c4a1–m3c4a3, m3c5: Original VHLSS module‑3 items on nonfarm employment, local economic activity, and social problems, providing commune‑level indicators of nonfarm jobs, business conditions, and related constraints used in constructing household‑business development outcomes.
roadvmonth: Measure of road or transport–related investment or maintenance at the commune level (e.g., months with road work or road access), capturing intensity of road service over the year.
totalhh: Total number of households in the commune, used to construct household shares for service coverage (e.g., share of households receiving agricultural extension or health fee support).
improve: Indicator summarizing whether overall living standards or socio‑economic conditions in the commune have improved over a recent period as reported by local authorities.
poorhh: Number or share of poor households in the commune according to official poverty classification, providing a commune‑level poverty rate.
geogra: Categorical or coded measure of the commune’s geographic type (e.g., lowland, highland, coastal, remote), used as a control for structural conditions in service delivery.
pro135: Indicator for whether the commune is covered by Vietnam’s Program 135 or other national poverty‑targeted programs, capturing exposure to special development support.
remotecom: Indicator for whether the commune is classified as remote or especially difficult, reflecting geographic disadvantage and higher costs of service provision.
credithh: Number or share of households receiving formal or semi‑formal credit support, used as an outcome in the household‑business development index.
povrate: Commune‑level poverty rate constructed from poor households over total households or from official statistics, summarizing local deprivation.
pro1–pro6: Set of indicators capturing the presence or implementation of different centrally funded socio‑economic projects or programs in the commune (e.g., transport, health, education, poverty alleviation), used to characterize local project activity.
agrext / dagrext: Indicators for the presence of agricultural extension services in the commune and changes over time (e.g., availability of extension staff or centers), feeding into the agricultural services index.
roadv / goodroadv / droadv: Measures of village‑level road access and quality, including whether villages are connected by all‑weather roads, the share of “good” roads, and changes in road conditions across years.
transport: Indicator for whether the commune has public transport services (e.g., bus or other collective transport), one of the treated infrastructure outcomes.
post / market / electricity / culture / broadcast / irrigation: Binary or categorical indicators for the presence of key public facilities in the commune—post offices, markets, electricity grid connections, cultural houses, broadcast stations, and irrigation systems—used as inputs to infrastructure and communications indices.
prischool / lseschool / useschool / kgarten: Indicators for the existence or accessibility of primary, lower‑secondary, upper‑secondary schools, and kindergartens in the commune, forming the base of the education services index.
nonfarm / nonfarme: Measures of nonfarm employment and nonfarm enterprises in the commune, capturing diversification of local livelihoods away from agriculture.
emproblem: Indicator summarizing key employment problems in the commune (e.g., underemployment, lack of local jobs) as reported by commune leaders.
migration_in / migration_out: Commune‑level counts or indicators for in‑migration and out‑migration, reflecting population flows and labor mobility.
population: Total population of the commune, used to scale services and to construct population density.
rm2c7a–rm2c7g (rm2c7a–rm2c7f, rm2c7g): Group of items capturing specific social or economic problems reported by commune authorities (e.g., crime, environmental issues, social evils), providing contextual information on local challenges.
villbusi / numbusi: Indicators for whether the commune has village‑level household businesses and the total number of household businesses, used in the household business development index.
agrrise: Indicator for whether agricultural production in the commune has recently risen, reflecting local economic trends in farming.
cleanwater / tapwater: Indicators for access to clean water sources and piped or tap water in the commune, often used as complementary infrastructure or health‑related outcomes.
agrvisit / plant_s / animal_s: Measures of agricultural extension intensity—such as the number of extension visits (agrvisit) and the presence of plant and animal husbandry support services—capturing the depth of agricultural support.
polluted: Indicator for whether the commune reports pollution problems, capturing environmental conditions that may co‑vary with infrastructure and industrialization.
nfworkers: Number of nonfarm workers in the commune workforce, summarizing structural change in local employment.
hecenter1–hecenter5, hecenter: Indicators for the existence of different types of local health centers or facilities and an aggregate indicator summarizing whether any such health center is present, feeding into the health services index.
d_hecenter1–d_hecenter5: Change indicators tracking whether specific types of health centers have appeared or disappeared between survey waves, capturing dynamics of health infrastructure.
lender1–lender7, lender1a–lender6a: Indicators for the presence or use of multiple types of credit providers in the commune (e.g., different institutional or informal lenders) and their activity, providing a detailed picture of local credit markets for households and small firms.
d_lender1–d_lender7, d_lender1a–d_lender6a: Change variables indicating expansions or contractions in access to the corresponding lender types over time, used to study evolution of credit access.
land1–land5: Areas or shares of different categories of agricultural land in the commune (e.g., by land type or use class), summarizing the structure of local land resources.
land1_irr / land2_irr: Portions of specific land categories under irrigation, measuring the intensity of irrigation infrastructure across agricultural land.
land1_cer–land5_cer: Areas of specific land categories devoted to cereal or staple crops, characterizing local cropping patterns.
vmarket1–vmarket3: Indicators for the existence of various kinds of markets within commune villages (e.g., daily, periodic, or wholesale), used in the household business development index.
vpeocom / vpost / vbank: Indicators for the presence of people’s committees, post offices, and bank or credit institutions within villages, capturing intra‑commune spatial distribution of administrative and financial services.
dmarket1–dmarket3 / dpeocom / dpost / dbank: Change indicators for village‑level markets, administrative offices, post offices, and banks, reflecting expansions or contractions in local service coverage over time.
dtown: Indicator for proximity to or inclusion of a district town within the commune, capturing centrality in the district’s spatial hierarchy.
timemarket1–timemarket3: Travel time measures from the commune or villages to different market types, providing continuous measures of market access.
v_prischool / v_lseschool / v_useschool: Indicators for the presence of primary, lower‑secondary, and upper‑secondary schools at the village level, refining the education access measures beyond commune‑level presence.
s_prischool / s_lseschool / s_useschool: Measures of schooling capacity or scale (e.g., number of classrooms or students) for primary, lower‑secondary, and upper‑secondary schools in the commune.
d_prischool / d_lseschool / d_useschool: Change indicators showing whether different school levels have opened or closed between survey waves.
year: Calendar year of the VHLSS commune survey (2006, 2008, 2010), forming the time dimension of the panel.
reg8: Eight‑region stratification code (e.g., Northern Mountains, Red River Delta, Central Coast, etc.) used to control for macro‑regional differences and to mirror the stratified design of the DPC abolition pilot.
commune: String or numeric identifier for the commune, harmonized to track the same locality across survey years.
province_name / district_name / tentinh / tinh_new: Text and alternative numeric codes for provinces and districts, allowing transparent labeling of administrative units and alignment with official administrative changes.
treatment: Indicator equal to 1 for communes in districts where District People’s Councils were abolished in the national pilot and 0 for communes in control districts, serving as the main treatment variable in the difference‑in‑differences design.
nongnghiep / congnghiep / dichvu: Province‑ or district‑level measures of agricultural, industrial, and service output or employment linked to communes, summarizing sectoral structure of the local economy.
laodong: Total labor force in the province or district associated with the commune, used to compute labor‑force‑based ratios.
danso: Total population at the higher administrative level, complementing the commune‑level population measure and providing a basis for relative shares.
time: Analysis time variable (e.g., coded 0/1 for pre‑ and post‑treatment) used in constructing interaction terms for difference‑in‑differences estimation.
totalland / sland1–sland5: Total agricultural land area in the commune and corresponding areas allocated to the same land categories as land1–land5, often expressed in standardized units to compare across communes.
area / lnarea: Commune land area in physical units and its natural logarithm, used to control for size and to compute densities.
popden / lnpopden: Population density (population per area) and its logarithm, capturing how densely settled the commune is.
lnnongnghiep / lncongnghiep / lndichvu: Natural logs of agricultural, industrial, and service output at the province or district level, used as covariates summarizing economic scale by sector.
lnlaodong / lndanso: Natural logs of labor force and population for the higher‑level administrative unit, providing scale controls in regressions.
rnongnghiep / rcongnghiep / rdichvu / rlaodong: Relative or share measures (e.g., ratios) of agriculture, industry, services, and labor force in the province or district, capturing economic structure rather than levels.
steering: Indicator for whether the commune lies in a province directly overseen by the national steering committee for the DPC removal pilot, allowing sensitivity checks for central oversight.
surveyed: Indicator for whether the province containing the commune was additionally visited and surveyed by the Ministry of Home Affairs evaluation teams, used to test for Hawthorne‑type monitoring effects.

name: The impact of intergenerational support on multidimensional poverty in old age: Empirical analysis based on 2018 CLHLS data
query: How does receiving economic support affect spiritual poverty?
dataset_description:
This study examines multidimensional poverty among senior citizens in China using data from the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS). The dataset contains individual-level observations with variables measuring demographic characteristics, household composition, and social support factors.

Variables:
economicsupport: The logarithm of the amount the children give to the parent
emotionalsupport: Indicator specifying whether one receives emotional support through conversations with children (1 = yes, 0 = no)
caresupport: Indicator specifying whether one is comfortable expressing their thoughts to children
gender: Respondent's gender (1 = male, 0 = female)
age: Respondent's age in years
squareofage: Age squared
maritalstatus: Marital status (1 = with spouse, 0 = no spouse)
householdregistration: Household registration (1 = urban, 0 = rural)
totalnumberofchildren: Total number of children in the household
numberofboys: Number of male children in the household
proportionofboys: Proportion of boys among all children
totalhouseholdincome: Total household income (log of annual income last year)
numberofpeoplelivingtogether: Number of people living in the household
region: Geographic region of the respondent (1 = eastern, 0 = not eastern)
socialsecurity: Whether the respondent has social security (1 = yes, 0 = no)
emotionalsupport: Whether the respondent receives emotional support (1 = yes, 0 = no)
multidimensionalpoverty: Multidimensional poverty status (1 = yes, 0 = no)
spiritualpoverty: Indicator denoting whether one feels lonely or not (1 = yes, 0 = no)
rightspoverty: Indicator denoting whether one has final say in their business or not (1 = yes, 0 = no)
economicpoverty: Indicator denoting whether the source of living is sufficient or not (1 = yes, 0 = no)
healthpoverty: Indicator denoting whether one is healthy or not (1 = yes, 0 = no)

name: Internet-accessed sexually transmitted infection (e-sti) testing and results service: A randomised, single-blind, controlled trial
query: What is the effect of the e-STI testing service on the probability of getting tested for an STI by 6 weeks?
dataset_description:
The data comes from a randomized control trial conducted to assess the impact of Internet-accessed sexually transmitted infection testing (e-STI testing) through the sh24 platform. Sexually active individuals between the ages of 16 and 30 were recruited. The participants were then randomly sent text messages inviting them to participate in the testing. The treatment group was asked to order the test online while the control group was asked to visit a walk-in clinic and take the test. The main outcome of interest was the self-reported diagnosis of STIs, supported by medical reports.

Variables include:
anon_id: Participant id
group: Allocation group ('Control' denotes control group and 'SH_24' denotes treatment group)
imd_decile: Index of Multiple Deprivation decile rankings on scale of 1-10; 1 represents the most deprived and 10 represents the least deprived
partners: Number of sexual partners in past 12 months at baseline
gender: Gender (Male or Female)
msm: Men who have sex with men ('msm'=Yes; 'other'=No; 99=Not Known)
ethnicgrp: Ethnic group
age: Age in completed years at baseline
anytest_sr: Binary variable indicating whether the participant self-reported the completion of the STI test or not (1=tested, 0=not tested)
anydiag_sr: Binary variable indicating whether the participant self-reported the diagnosis of STI test or not (1=diagnosed, 0=not diagnosed)
anytreat_sr: Binary variable indicating whether the participant self-reported receiving STI treatment or not (1=treated, 0=not treated)
anytest: Objectively verified binary indicator of STI testing completion (1 = tested, 0 = not tested)
anydiag: Objectively verified binary indicator of STI diagnosis (1 = diagnosed, 0 = not diagnosed)
anytreat: Objectively verified binary indicator of STI treatment (1 = treated, 0 = not treated)
time_test: Time from randomization to test in days
time_treat: Time from randomization to treatment in days
sh24_launch: Binary variable indicating whether the randomization occurred before or after SH:24 was made publicly available (1 = yes, 0 = no)

name: Estimating incumbency effects using regression discontinuity design
query: In the UK, in very close elections, does just barely winning make it more likely that the party's candidate will stand again as the incumbent in the next election?
dataset_description:
The dataset is a panel of electoral constituencies across multiple countries and years, designed to study incumbency effects. Each row corresponds to a party's performance in a given constituency at a given election.

Dataset Variables:
year: The year of the election
country: The country where the election took place (e.g., Canada, Japan, UK, USA, Romania, etc.)
office: Name of the office being contested (e.g., House of Commons, Mayor)
cst_n: Constituency identifier (e.g., ""abbotsford"", ""abitibi"")
l_vmargin: Lagged vote margin: the party's vote margin in the previous election (Values more than 0 indicate the party won (positive) and values less than 0 indicate the party lost (negative))
vmargin: Current vote margin: the party's vote margin in the current election
vs: Vote share of the party in the current election (between 0 and 1)
win: Outcome of the current election: 1 means the party won the seat, 0 means the party lost
l_win: Lagged win indicator: 1 means the party won the previous election in this constituency, 0 means the party lost
inc: Incumbency indicator for the party's candidate in the current election: 1 means candidate is the incumbent, 0 means not incumbent, -1 appears to mark cases where incumbency is undefined or missing
office_num: Encoded office type, combining country and office (e.g., Canada, House)
rd_s: Indicator variable that equals 1 if the observation is part of a subset of elections defined by narrow vote margins, and 0 otherwise

name: Vouchers for private schooling in Colombia: Evidence from a randomized natural experiment
query: Does winning a voucher affect whether students get married a few years later?
dataset_description:
This dataset is an individual-level microdata file on applicants to Colombia's PACES secondary-school voucher program, combining lottery assignment records, follow-up survey responses, and achievement test participation indicators for cohorts in Bogota (1995, 1997) and Jamundi (1993). It is structured to support analysis of schooling trajectories, private versus public school attendance, household background, labor and family formation outcomes, and test-taking behavior for voucher-eligible youth, without embedding specific modeling choices.

Variables include:

ID: Numeric identifier linking each record to the original PACES applicant list, stable within the file and used to join administrative lottery status, survey outcomes, and test participation.
BOG95SMP: Indicator for membership in the Bogota 1995 applicant cohort analysis sample (1 = Bogota 1995 cohort, 0 otherwise), aligning each individual with that specific city-year sampling frame.
BOG97SMP: Indicator for membership in the Bogota 1997 applicant cohort analysis sample (1 = Bogota 1997 cohort, 0 otherwise), distinguishing this later application year within Bogota.
JAM93SMP: Indicator for membership in the Jamundi 1993 applicant cohort analysis sample (1 = Jamundi 1993 cohort, 0 otherwise), identifying applicants from the suburban Cali site.
SEX: Binary sex indicator at the individual level, derived from survey or name-based coding and used for gender-disaggregated description and outcome analysis.
AGE: Applicant's age in completed years, typically imputed from the Colombian national ID at the time of program application and used as a key demographic control.
AGE2: Square of age, capturing non-linear relationships between age and schooling outcomes or other behaviors such as work and marriage.
HSVISIT: Indicator for interview mode (1 = household visit, 0 = telephone interview), reflecting fieldwork logistics and used to control for mode-related response differences.
SCYFNSH: Measure summarizing schooling completion within the secondary cycle (for example, highest grade completed by survey date), constructed from detailed grade histories.
INSCHL: Binary indicator for current school enrollment at the survey date (1 = currently in school, 0 = not enrolled), derived from self-reported enrollment status.
PRSCH_C: Binary indicator for current private secondary school attendance (1 = enrolled in a private school at survey time, 0 = public school or not enrolled), used to describe current sector of schooling.
PRSCHA_1: Indicator capturing private-school attendance at a key grade or early stage of secondary schooling (1 = attended a participating private secondary school at that stage, 0 otherwise), constructed from retrospective schooling histories.
PRSCHA_2: Complementary indicator for private-school attendance at an additional grade or later stage of secondary schooling, allowing distinctions between initial and subsequent private enrollment episodes.
VOUCH0: Binary lottery-assignment indicator for the PACES voucher offer (1 = offered a PACES scholarship via lottery, 0 = not offered), taken from administrative lottery records and used to distinguish voucher winners from losers.
BOG95ASD: Indicator for inclusion in the Bogota 1995 achievement-test subsample (1 = invited/test sample for Bogota 1995, 0 otherwise), identifying records with linked standardized test scores.
BOG97ASD: Indicator for inclusion in any Bogota 1997 achievement-related subsample if present, parallel in structure to BOG95ASD but for the 1997 cohort.
JAM93ASD: Indicator for inclusion in any Jamundi 1993 achievement-test subsample if collected, flagging Jamundi test-takers within the broader applicant frame.
DBOGOTA: City dummy for Bogota (1 = Bogota, 0 = other sites), aligning individuals with the capital city context for descriptive and regression controls.
DJAMUNDI: City dummy for Jamundi (1 = Jamundi, 0 = other sites), capturing the suburban Cali site as distinct from Bogota.
D1995: Application-year dummy (1 = applied in 1995, 0 otherwise), marking the Bogota 1995 cohort in pooled analyses across years.
D1997: Application-year dummy (1 = applied in 1997, 0 otherwise), identifying the later Bogota cohort in multi-cohort analyses.
D1993: Application-year dummy (1 = applied in 1993, 0 otherwise), corresponding to the Jamundi 1993 cohort.
RESPONSE: Indicator that a valid 1998 follow-up survey interview was completed for the applicant (1 = interviewed, 0 = in sampling frame but not interviewed), capturing differential follow-up.
TEST_TAK: Indicator that the applicant took the 1999 standardized achievement test (1 = test-taker, 0 = not tested), linking survey records to test-score availability.
SEX_NAME: Auxiliary indicator of sex coded from first names in the application list, used to impute sex where direct survey information is missing.
SVY: Survey-form or instrument indicator that flags the questionnaire version or survey group, enabling control for minor differences in question wording or survey conditions.
PHONE: Indicator for having a telephone contact at application (1 = phone number recorded, 0 = no phone), reflecting contactability and part of the implicit sampling frame for telephone interviews.
DAREA1-DAREA19: Set of neighborhood or large-area dummies for Bogota (and analogous groupings where applicable), capturing 19 residential areas used as geographic strata or controls.
DMONTH1-DMONTH12: Interview-month dummies (1 = interviewed in the corresponding calendar month, 0 otherwise), representing survey timing over the fieldwork period.
BOG95: Indicator for being in the Bogota 1995 cohort in contexts where this cohort is contrasted with others, often overlapping conceptually with BOG95SMP but used in some outcome subsamples.
BOG97: Indicator for being in the Bogota 1997 cohort, similarly used as a cohort marker in pooled models.
MOM_SCH: Mother's highest completed grade of schooling in years, as reported in the survey, serving as a parental human-capital measure.
MOM_AGE: Mother's age in years at the time of survey, capturing parental lifecycle stage.
MOM_MW: Indicator that the mother's wage exceeds a threshold multiple of the minimum wage (for example, more than two minimum wages), proxying maternal earnings capacity.
DAD_SCH: Father's highest completed grade of schooling in years, measuring paternal education as part of family background.
DAD_AGE: Father's age in years at the time of survey, capturing paternal lifecycle stage.
DAD_MW: Indicator that the father's wage exceeds a threshold multiple of the minimum wage, summarizing paternal earnings potential.
SEX2: Harmonized or alternative sex indicator used in the main analytic regressions, combining name-based and survey-based sex coding where necessary.
STRATA1-STRATA6: Set of dummies for the six official Colombian socioeconomic residential strata, derived from utility-bill based classification in the application and used to capture household socioeconomic status.
STRATAMS: Indicator for missing or unspecified socioeconomic stratum, preserving individuals with incomplete strata information in analyses.
REPT6: Indicator that the applicant repeated sixth grade at least once, summarizing early grade repetition at the entry to secondary schooling.
TOTSCYRS: Total number of calendar years spent in school since the time of application, aggregating enrollment histories into a duration-style schooling exposure measure.
HASCHILD: Indicator that the applicant has at least one child at the time of survey, measuring early fertility outcomes.
MARRIED: Indicator that the applicant is married or cohabiting with a partner at the time of survey, capturing early union formation.
WORKING: Binary indicator that the applicant is engaged in paid work at the time of survey, summarizing labor-force participation.
REPT: Indicator that the applicant has repeated at least one grade after the lottery, capturing any post-application grade repetition.
NREPT: Count of grades repeated since the lottery, providing a more granular measure of cumulative repetition.
FINISH6: Indicator that the applicant has successfully completed grade 6, the first year of Colombian secondary school.
FINISH7: Indicator that the applicant has successfully completed grade 7, reflecting progression through early secondary schooling.
FINISH8: Indicator that the applicant has successfully completed grade 8, used to summarize lower-secondary completion.
SEX_MISS: Indicator that sex information is missing in the primary coding, flagging records relying on imputation or with unresolved sex classification.
USNGSCH: Indicator that the applicant is using any scholarship (PACES voucher or other scholarship) in the survey year, capturing current scholarship utilization.
HOURSUM: Total number of hours worked per week by the applicant at the time of survey, computed from reported work schedules and used to quantify labor supply.
TAB3SMPL: Indicator that an observation is included in the analysis sample corresponding to a specific table (for example, Table 3) in the original study, marking the main balanced analytic subsample.
WORKING3: Alternative working-status indicator defined for the Table 3 sample or using a particular coding of work (e.g., excluding very low-intensity work), complementing WORKING.

REPT6: Indicator that the applicant repeated sixth grade at least once, summarizing early grade repetition at the entry to secondary schooling.

HASCHILD: Indicator that the applicant has at least one child at the time of survey, measuring early fertility outcomes.

REPT: Indicator that the applicant has repeated at least one grade after the lottery, capturing any post-application grade repetition.

SEX_MISS: Indicator that sex information is missing in the primary coding, flagging records relying on imputation or with unresolved sex classification.
USNGSCH: Indicator that the applicant is using any scholarship (PACES voucher or other scholarship) in the survey year, capturing current scholarship utilization.
HOURSUM: Total number of hours worked per week by the applicant at the time of survey, computed from reported work schedules and used to quantify labor supply.
TAB3SMPL: Indicator that an observation is included in the analysis sample corresponding to a specific table (for example, Table 3) in the original study, marking the main balanced analytic subsample.
WORKING3: Alternative working-status indicator defined for the Table 3 sample or using a particular coding of work (e.g., excluding very low-intensity work), complementing WORKING.

name: Instrumental variables estimates of the effect of subsidized training on the quantiles of trainee earnings

dataset_description:
This dataset was constructed to measure how subsidized Job Training Partnership Act (JTPA) programs affect not just average earnings but different points (quantiles) of the trainee earnings distribution. Data collection process: Data are drawn from the National JTPA Study - a large encouragement design randomized controlled trial under the JTPA. Eligible individuals were randomly assigned to be offered training services (treatment group) or excluded for 18 months (control group), with roughly 60% of those offered actually receiving training. Baseline demographic and economic covariates were collected before randomization, and earnings plus participation data were tracked for 30 months post-assignment via administrative records and follow-up interviews.

name: Field experiments testing the impact of radio advertisements on electoral competition
query: What was the effect of the radio advertising campaign on the change in the incumbent mayor's vote share in the 2006 elections?
dataset_description:
The dataset consists of 49 observations from mayoral elections in U.S. cities, with 33 observations from 2005 and 16 from 2006. The data is gathered through a randomized field experiment. Within matched pairs of municipalities, one city was randomly assigned to the treatment group and the other to the control group. The treatment involved a 60-second, non-partisan get-out-the-vote radio advertisement. The control group received no such intervention. The unit of observation is the city. Inclusion was limited to cities with populations over 30,000 where an incumbent mayor ran for reelection against an opponent. The study's outcome measure is the change in the incumbent mayor's vote share compared to the previous election.

name: Does rising income inequality affect mortality rates in advanced economies?
query: Does a greater inequality in income lead to a higher average mortality rate among males and females?
dataset_description:
This dataset aims to study the effect of income inequality on mortality rates for men and women in a subset of OECD countries from 1950 to 2000 using adult mortality rates at age sixty-five as the measure of mortality. Likewise, for measuring income inequality, the inverted Pareto-Lorenz coefficient was used. The coefficient is directly obtained from the World Top Income Database. More specifically, the measure was derived from individual taxation and income data as well as national account statistics. The Pareto-Lorenz coefficient ranges from 1.5 to 3. Values in the range of 1.5 to 1.8 are considered low inequality, while values above 2.5 are considered high inequality.

Data variables:
year: Year observation was taken
cc: Country code
qxall: Averaged rate between qxfemale and qxmale
qxfemale: Five-year mortality rate for females at age sixty-five (the probability of dying within 5 years for 65-year-old women)
invertedplc: Inverted Pareto-Lorenz coefficient (measure of income inequality at the top end of distribution, ranging from ~1.5-3)
exfemale: Life expectancy for females at age 65
qxmale: Five-year mortality rate for males at age sixty-five (the probability of dying within 5 years for 65-year-old men)
exmale: Life expectancy for males (at age 65)
country: Country name
rgdpe: Real GDP obtained from Penn World Table; values adjusted for purchasing power parity
pop: Population (in millions)
hc: Health capital index - a measure capturing educational attainment that serves as a proxy for human capital stock
rpcgdp: Real per capita GDP - GDP per person adjusted for purchasing power parity

This dataset combines municipal-level information from across France to study the political effects of migrant relocation after the dismantling of the Calais ""Jungle"" between 2015 and 2016. Data on temporary migrant reception centers, called Centres d'Accueil et d'Orientation (CAOs), were collected through a combination of systematic searches in local newspapers using Factiva and a publicly released dataset by CIMADE in October 2016. The media search recorded CAO locations and migrant counts reported in articles, while the CIMADE dataset listed 210 centers and their capacities. name: The global costs of extreme weather that are attributable to climate change
query: How much of global total economic damages due to extreme weather is attributable to climate change? (in thousands)
dataset_description:
The study examines the global economic costs of extreme weather events attributable to climate change using Event Attribution methodology. It analyzes 185 extreme weather events from 2000-2019 across multiple countries, combining data from climate attribution studies with socio-economic impact data from the Emergency Management Database (EM-DAT). The methodology uses climate models to compare observed extreme weather events with counterfactual scenarios without anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. This generates Fraction of Attributable Risk (FAR) estimates quantifying what portion of each event's risk is attributable to human-induced climate change. These FAR values are then applied to observed mortality and economic damages to calculate climate change-attributable costs globally.

Variable description:
- Event Identifier: Identifies the specific extreme weather event
- Year: Year of event
- Country/region: Country of event
- Continent: Continent where event happened
- Disaster Type: One of Flood, Heatwave, Wildfire, Drought, Storm, Cold wave
- FAR Best Estimate: FAR value = 1 - p_1/p_0, where p_1 is the probability of event in the real world, and p_0 in counterfactual world without climate change.
- Total Deaths: Total number of deaths caused by event
- Total Affected
- Total Damage (US$ Thousands): Amount of damage caused in thousands of US dollars per event
- Insured Loss (US$ Thousands): Amount of economic damage insured
- Uninsured damages: Difference of previous two
- Total Damage (US$ Millions): Amount of damage caused in millions of US dollars per event
- Insured Loss (US$ Millions): Amount of economic damage insured (in millions)

name: A Call to Arms: How Rebel Groups Choose Their Recruitment Appeals
query: Does being a radical Islamist group causally increase the number of recruitment appeals they make?
dataset_description:
This dataset is a cross-sectional rebel-group-level file that integrates original measures of recruitment appeals from the Rebel Appeals and Incentives Dataset (RAID) with standardized indicators of rebel ideology, organizational features, and country-level context for 232 rebel movements active worldwide between 1989 and 2011. Each record corresponds to a distinct rebel organization and captures both the breadth and composition of its grievance-based recruitment appeals, as well as its ideological profile, strength, territorial control, ethnic composition, and the regime and economic environment in which it operates.

Variable descriptions
new_side_b_id: Numeric group identifier that uniquely references each rebel organization in the merged file, harmonizing the RAID units with the underlying non-state actor and replication identifiers used for statistical analysis.
ccode: Numeric country code indicating the primary state within which the rebel group is active, enabling linkage to country-level democracy and GDP covariates and the clustering of standard errors by conflict country.
ideol_ord: Ordinal indicator capturing the group’s core ideology type as used in the models (e.g., distinguishing radical Islamist from other ideological families) to operationalize the main explanatory contrast in the paper.
other_rel_appeals: Dichotomous RAID-based indicator coded 1 if the group sometimes employs recruitment appeals to non-Islamist religious ideologies (e.g., generic religious or non-radical faith-based claims), and 0 otherwise.
left_appeals: Binary variable denoting whether the group recruits using left-wing or communist ideological appeals, such as references to Marxist principles or anti-capitalist class struggle.
anti_resource_appeals: Indicator coded 1 when rebel recruitment materials highlight opposition to the exploitation of local resources by external actors, including grievances about plunder or unequal resource extraction.
gov_violence_appeals: Binary measure for appeals centered on violent government repression and human rights abuses, where recruitment narratives emphasize state-perpetrated killings, torture, or indiscriminate attacks.
feminist_appeals: Indicator for appeals invoking women’s rights or gender inequality as a recruitment theme, such as mobilizing against gendered exclusion or violence.
other_appeals: Catch-all binary category capturing miscellaneous recruitment appeals that do not fit the primary ideological or grievance types but nonetheless appear as recurring frames in the group’s propaganda.
ethnic_nat_appeals: Dichotomous RAID measure indicating whether the group mobilizes recruits using ethnonationalist or regional grievances, such as discrimination against a specific ethnic community or demands for national self-determination.
anti_intervention_appeals: Binary indicator coded 1 when groups employ recruitment appeals opposing foreign military intervention or occupation, including denunciations of external troops or international coalitions.
gov_grievance_appeals: Variable marking general anti-government grievance appeals, where recruitment emphasizes corruption, misrule, or broad political injustices without being limited to a single policy issue.
multi_ethnic: Dichotomous measure from RAID indicating whether the group’s membership is multi-ethnic, capturing heterogeneity in the ethnic background of recruits rather than whether ethnicity is the explicit basis of mobilization.
secessionist: Binary indicator of whether the organization has secessionist aims, that is, whether it seeks to create an independent state separate from the existing central government.
reb_strength_ord: Ordinal measure of relative rebel strength taken from the NSA dataset, capturing expert assessments of whether the group is weaker, roughly equal, or stronger relative to government forces.
name: Text string with the full or commonly used name of the rebel organization, preserving interpretable labels alongside numeric identifiers for substantive interpretation and replication.
multi_appeals: Binary summary indicator coded 1 if the group uses two or more distinct recruitment appeals (across the RAID dimensions), operationalizing whether recruitment is diversified versus narrow.
terr_cont: Dichotomous measure for whether the group controls territory at any point, indicating de facto governance or sustained physical control of areas as captured in the NSA data.
any_nr_binary: Indicator for whether the group exploited any natural resources (e.g., lootable or extractive commodities) during its life, derived from the Rebel Contraband Dataset and collapsed into a yes/no measure.
appeals_count: Count variable measuring the total number of distinct recruitment appeals coded for the group across the RAID dimensions, ranging from 0 (no grievance-based appeals, only material incentives) to higher values for groups with more diverse appeals.
other_group_binary: Binary measure capturing whether another rebel group was present in the same country when this group entered the armed conflict dataset, providing a simple indicator of inter-rebel competition.
left_wing: Dichotomous indicator (from WARD/FORGE) for whether the organization has a communist or broader left-wing founding ideology, used both as a control and for constructing alternative measures of ideological diversity.
supporttype_funds_rebel: Binary variable indicating whether the group received financial support from external actors (e.g., state sponsors or foreign patrons), based on external support data on rebel funding.
radical_islamist: Core binary explanatory variable coded 1 for groups with a radical Islamist ideology—those espousing goals such as establishing an Islamic state, enforcing religious law, or defending Islam—and 0 otherwise.
foreign_f: Dichotomous indicator of whether the group recruits foreign fighters, based on external foreign-fighter datasets and used to test how internationalization of recruitment conditions appeal diversity.
v2x_polyarchy: Continuous country-level democracy score (polyarchy index) for the group’s main country, capturing the extent of electoral competition and participation and serving as a control for regime type.
mean_log10_gdp_pc: Continuous measure of average logged GDP per capita in the group’s host country over its active period, capturing income levels and included as a macroeconomic control.
group_age: Numeric variable measuring the age or duration of the group (e.g., years active), used as a control to account for the possibility that older organizations have had more time to diversify appeals.
ideology_forge_count: Count of the number of distinct founding ideologies attributed to the group in the FORGE dataset (e.g., religious, nationalist, left-wing), used in robustness checks on broader ideological diversity.
incompatible_appeals: Binary measure constructed by examining all pairwise correlations among appeals in RAID and coding 1 if the group employs at least one pair of appeals that are negatively and significantly associated in the full sample, indicating that it combines appeals most groups avoid mixing.
post_2003: Dichotomous indicator taking value 1 for groups active after 2003, capturing the post–Iraq invasion period in which transnational jihadist dynamics and perceptions of threats to Islam intensified.
ideology_count: Count variable summarizing the number of ideologies a group represents across external ideology datasets (e.g., socialism, Islamism, nationalism), used in robustness checks on ideological diversification beyond recruitment appeals.
appeals_count_restrict: Alternative, more restrictive count of recruitment appeals that excludes appeals corresponding to the group’s parent ideology (e.g., omitting Islamist appeals for Islamist groups), used to test whether results hold when focusing on “non-core” grievances.
multi_appeals_restrict: Binary version of the restrictive count, coded 1 if the group makes two or more non-parent appeals, allowing analyses of diversified grievance framing net of primary ideology.
year_start: Calendar year in which the group first appears in the armed conflict or non-state actor data, anchoring the onset of its conflict activity and the period over which contextual covariates are averaged or coded.
year_end: Calendar year in which the group exits the dataset (e.g., due to dissolution, defeat, or end of recorded activity), marking the end of its observed life span for the purposes of computing group age and averaging country-level variables.

query: What is the effect of being drafted on the compliers among those who comply with the draft lottery, explained by serving in the military, with respect to holding mild democrat views?
dataset_description:
The study analyzes the impact of the Vietnam draft lottery on political preferences, recognizing that lottery assignment may have influenced attitudes through multiple channels beyond military service alone. Not everyone chosen by the lottery actually served, creating variation in both draft exposure and service status. 
Interviews were conducted in wave 4 (prior to July 1, 1970 lottery) and wave 5 (spring 1974), allowing examination of attitude changes over time. Each row contains an individual's political preferences in a given wave. Focus on waves 4 and 5. 
The direct effect captures how lottery assignment affected political preferences independent of military service—through heightened political awareness, life planning changes, or social identity shifts. The indirect effect operates through actual military service experience.

repu: whether the individual describes themselves as a mild republican

name: Experimental evidence that changing beliefs about mask efficacy and social norms increase mask wearing for covid-19 risk reduction: Results from the United states and Italy
query: How much does greater mask use increase the likelihood that someone would encourage others to wear a mask?
dataset_description:
The randomized experiment examines the causal relationship between beliefs, social norms, and reported intentions to engage in mask promoting behavior.
Subjects are randomly assigned to a control group, a ""Mask Protects You"" group, and a ""Mask Protects Others"" group.
The control group reads a message unrelated to the experiment, the ""Mask Protects You"" group reads a message about how masks protect the wearer, and the ""Mask Protects Others"" group reads a message about how masks protect others.
After the treatment, subjects are asked about their beliefs about masks.
They then read three vignette scenarios, taking place at an ATM, in a park or in a meeting in their neighborhood.
In the first scenario, they are asked about what they would do when they have forgotten to bring their mask. In the second scenario, they are asked about what they would do if someone else was not wearing their mask properly. In the third scenario, they are asked about their evaluation of someone who took action against someone not wearing their mask properly.

Variables in the dataset:

age: age of the subject
female: whether the subject is female
lucid_hhi: household income
lucid_incmissing: whether the subject's income is missing
ethnicity: ethnicity of the subject
education: education level of the subject
workstatus: work status of the subject
fluvaccine: whether the subject has received the flu vaccine
pool_self_scenario_atm: whether the first vignette scenario takes place at an ATM
pool_self_scenario_meet: whether the first vignette scenario takes place in a meeting in the neighborhood
pool_other_scenario_atm: whether the second vignette scenario takes place at an ATM
pool_other_scenario_meet: whether the second vignette scenario takes place in a meeting in the neighborhood
partisanship_1: whether the subject is a strong democrat
partisanship_2: whether the subject is a democrat
partisanship_3: whether the subject is a democrat lean
partisanship_4: whether the subject is an independent
partisanship_5: whether the subject is a republican lean
partisanship_6: whether the subject is a republican
partisanship_7: whether the subject is a strong republican
T_mask_protectyou: whether the subject was in the ""Mask Protects You"" group
T_mask_protectother: whether the subject was in the ""Mask Protects Others"" group
mskblfs_prtctothers: whether the subject believes that masks protect others after the intervention
mskblfs_prtctyou: whether the subject believes that masks protect the wearer after the intervention
pool_self: own mask wearing behavior in the vignette scenario, 1 means they would continue the activity without a mask, 2 means they would continue the activity without a mask while keeping distance from others, 3 means they would abandon the activity, 4 means they would go retrieve their mask and then continue the activity
pool_other: behavior when someone else is not wearing their mask properly, 1 means they would continue the activity as normal, 2 means they would continue the activity as normal while keeping distance from others, 3 means they would abandon the activity, 4 means they would ask the other person to wear the mask properly
pool_self_others: whether others are wearing masks in the first vignette scenario
pool_other_others: whether others are wearing masks in the second vignette scenario

name: Cities as lobbyists
query: How much does the money spent on lobbying increase the received amount of recovery act grants?
dataset_description:
The dataset assembles city-level information on lobbying, federal resource allocation, connectivity to Washington, DC, and local demographic, fiscal, and political context for 1,262 U.S. cities with populations over 25,000 between 1999 and 2012. It links lobbying disclosures filed under the Lobbying Disclosure Act to Census/ACS demographics, Census of Governments fiscal data, federal earmark records, and airline route information to study how variation in public-goods provision and political environment relates to cities’ lobbying behavior and the earmarks they receive.

Variables in the dataset
id: Internal numeric identifier for each city in the replication dataset released with the article.
city: Name of the city (municipal government) included in the sample of U.S. cities with population above 25,000.
state: U.S. state in which the city is located, used to link to state-level fiscal and political data.
direct_flight_dc: Indicator for whether there is at least one direct commercial flight between the city’s local (or nearby) airport and any of the Washington, DC–area airports (BWI, DCA, or IAD) in the relevant period, capturing the convenience of travel to the capital and used as an instrument for city lobbying expenditures.
earmark: Total dollar amount of federal congressional earmarks awarded to the city in fiscal years 2008 and 2009, typically summed across those years and expressed in constant (2012) dollars.
city_lobbying: Total federal lobbying expenditures by the city government, based on Lobbying Disclosure Act reports, aggregated over the analysis window (e.g., around 2007–2009) and inflation-adjusted, with this variable serving as the core measure of city lobbying effort (often log-transformed in analysis).
state_lobbying: Total lobbying expenditures by the state government over a comparable period, providing a measure of higher-level governmental lobbying that may complement or compete with city efforts.
county_lobbying: Total lobbying expenditures by the county government in which the city is located, used to capture additional substate lobbying that can affect how much federal funding ultimately flows to the city (and is found to be negatively related to city earmarks and grants).
pop_e: City population, drawn from the Decennial Census and ACS and extrapolated to match the analysis years, providing a size control for lobbying and earmark outcomes.
land_e: Land area of the city (in square miles), as reported by Census geography files and used as a basic geographic control.
water_e: Water area of the city (in square miles), capturing the extent of water within city boundaries, again from Census geography data.
senior_e: Share of the city population aged 65 or older, constructed from Census/ACS age distributions and extrapolated to the analysis years.
student_e: Share of residents enrolled in school, capturing educational-age composition and demand for education-related public goods.
ethnic_e: Index of ethnic heterogeneity (ethnic fractionalization) at the city level, typically constructed from Census/ACS racial and ethnic composition using a fractionalization formula where higher values indicate more ethnically diverse cities, which the paper links to public-goods provision and lobbying.
mincome_e: Median household income in the city (often in thousands of dollars), measured using Census/ACS and extrapolated to the relevant period as an indicator of overall economic status.
unemp_e: City unemployment rate, capturing local labor-market conditions that may influence fiscal stress and demand for federal resources.
poverty_e: Share of households in poverty in the city, reflecting economic disadvantage and potential demand for redistributive public goods.
gini_e: Gini coefficient of income inequality at the city level, measuring the extent of income dispersion and used in the paper as a key determinant of lobbying behavior.
city_taxshare_e: Share of total city revenue coming from own-source taxes (summed across tax instruments), capturing how reliant the city is on its own tax base rather than external transfers.
city_propertytaxshare_e: Share of total city revenue specifically derived from property taxes, reflecting dependence on the property tax base and related fiscal capacity.
city_intgovrevenueshare_e: Share of total city revenue coming from intergovernmental transfers (state and federal), measuring how much of the city’s budget is financed by higher-level governments rather than local sources.
houdem_e: Indicator that the city’s U.S. House representative (in the district containing the city) is a Democrat, based on congressional delegation data matched via county–district crosswalks.
sendem_e: Indicator that at least one of the state’s U.S. Senators representing the city is a Democrat, capturing partisan alignment with the federal legislature.
govdem_e: Indicator that the state’s governor is a Democrat, capturing partisan control at the state executive level, which is theorized to affect state support for local public goods.
diverge1_e: First measure of the “public goods gap” between city and state, defined as the difference between the city’s direct expenditures per capita and the corresponding state government’s direct expenditures per capita, capturing how much more (or less) the city spends than the state overall.
diverge2_e: Second measure of the “public goods gap,” defined as the difference between the city’s direct expenditures per capita and the per capita state transfers to that city, measuring the portion of city spending not covered by state government support.
st_airexp_e: Per-capita state government expenditure on air transportation and related functions (from the Census of Governments), used as a state-level control related to air infrastructure that may correlate with the presence of airports and airline routes.
city_airexp_e: Per-capita city expenditure on air transportation (e.g., airports and related infrastructure), providing a city-level measure of investment in air facilities and helping to account for baseline air-service conditions when using direct flights as an instrument.

Year: Election Year
State: US state abbreviation
Chamber: Whether the election is for the House (H) or the Senate (S)

womanwon: Binary variable indicating whether a woman won the election or not (1 = Won, 0 = Lost)

femaleonballotnextyear: Share of women on the next election, i.e., women's voter turnout

name: The causal effect of radical right success on mainstream parties policy positions. A regression discontinuity approach

dataset_description:
The dataset aims to analyze the effect of radical right parties on the policy positions of the mainstream parties. It includes information on political parties belonging to various European countries, including their positions on cultural protectionism and environmental protectionism. Thresholds vary by country, so in this dataset, we used voter shares centered around the threshold.

name: Does earmarked funding affect the performance of international organisations?
query: How much does earmarked funding affect the performance of international organisations?
dataset_description:
The dataset compiles performance evaluations of 32 international organizations (IOs) from 2009 to 2021, encompassing 64 assessments conducted by the Multilateral Organization Performance Assessment Network (MOPAN). Organizations vary significantly in their funding composition, with some receiving predominantly core contributions that provide operational flexibility, while others rely heavily on earmarked resources that restrict fund usage to specific purposes, sectors, or geographic areas. Due to their specific nature, earmarked funding does not offer flexibility. Thus, there is a possibility that earmarked funding may limit organizational performance. The dataset tracks both short-term and long-term earmarked funding patterns alongside core funding levels. International organizations' performance is given by two metrics: 1) Process performance, the extent to which organizations have rules to plan and manage operations strategically, and 2) outcome performance, which measures the organization's success in achieving desired results.

Variables:
organization: international organization name
acronym: organization abbreviation
year: assessment year
mopan: The version of MOPAN methodology used in the assessment (one of 3.0, 3.1, or 3.0*, CA = older version)
newmopan: Binary variable that is 1 if the new MOPAN assessment methodology was used
y1: process performance factor score
y2: outcome performance factor score
y1n: process performance factor score after removing 2 micro indicators
y2n: outcome performance factor score after removing 2 micro indicators
EMST: earmarked funding share in the year before MOPAN assessment (t-1 year)
EMLT: earmarked funding share in the years t-2 and t-3 before MOPAN assessment, i.e., 2 and 3 years before
un: indicator for UN system organizations (1 = UN organization, 0 = non-UN organization)
coreSTd: non-core funding amount
coreST: core funding amount
emST: earmarked funding amount
emST_MBI: earmarked funding amount computed by MOPAN
emshareLTd: Share of earmarked funding in the IO budget based on data from UN DESA Data
emshareLTb: Share of earmarked funding in the IO budget based on data from UN Data Cube
emshareLT: Share of earmarked funding share for long-term projects
nproj_lt: number of earmarked projects
ndon_lt: number of donors providing earmarked funding
states_num: number of member states
states_unga_sd: standard deviation of the preferences of the member states with respect to ideal point estimates
tenure: executive head tenure length
selectorate: Variable indicating how the executive is selected (1 = appointed by the chief of parent organization, 2 = selected by the board, 3 = chosen by the assembly of member states)
founding: organization founding year
hq: headquarters location
field_presence: number of staff in the field
staff_count: total staff size
normio: indicator for norm-making IOs: FAO, ILO, UNESCO, UNHCR, UNIDO, WHO, GEF
lnsectors: logarithm of the number of sectors in which the organization receives donor funding
meanwSIM: weighted mean cosine similarity of sector-specific contribution profile, which is proportional to the total budget of the IOs

name: Cabinets, committees, and careers: The causal effect of committee service
query: What is the effect of being appointed to the budget committee on the probability a deputy sponsors a budget amendment within the next five years?
dataset_description:
The dataset comes from French parliamentary records across multiple legislative sessions. It is structured by deputy-year, and includes variables for legislative behavior, career success, policy-making, tenure, and constituent characteristics. An interesting feature of the lower house was that the legislature was randomly assigned into 11 groups called bureaux, and each group chose members to serve on the budget committee. The deputies convened with their assigned group, and after hours of discussion, each bureau nominated three representatives to serve on the budget committee. Bureaux was a temporary committee, and the selection was done every year. This random selection of bureaux (or bureau) for budget selection was done from 1894 to 1910, after which it was disbanded.

Variable description:
id: ID number (Unique identifier for each deputy)
year: Year (1894-1909)
term: Term (1893, 1898, 1902, or 1906)
leader: Deputy was any type of party leader (defined as a member of a parliamentary governing committee) (1 = yes, 0 = no)
centrist_all: Deputy was a member of a Radical or Radical-Socialist party (1 = Radical socialist, 0 = radical party)
inscrits: Number of electors in deputy's district (in 000s)
permargin: Electoral margin of prior election, as a ratio of total votes cast
paris: Whether the deputy represents a Parisian district or suburb (1 = Parisian district, 0 = suburb)
age: Age of deputy
bureau: Deputy's bureau number (assignment) for that year
budget: Deputy was on the budget committee (1 = yes, 0 = no)
min: Deputy was a minister (1 = yes, 0 = no)
termyear: Identifier for term + year
budgettermyears: Number of years a deputy has served on the budget committee, including the current year
budgetexptermyears: Budget experience in years
proprietaire: Deputy was a property owner (upper class) (1 = yes, 0 = no)
lib_all: Deputy held a liberal profession (middle class) (1 = yes, 0 = no)
civil: Deputy was a civil servant (1 = yes, 0 = no)
reelect: Deputy was reelected the next term (1 = yes, 0 = no)
F1to5firstminyear: Became a minister for the first time within 5 years (1 = yes, 0 = no)
F1to5firstleaderyear: Became a party leader within 5 years (1 = yes, 0 = no)
cummyears: Years of parliamentary experience
clburyear: Identifier for term year + bureau
budgetincumbent: Deputy was a budget incumbent (1 = yes, 0 = no)
bureauotherbudgetincumbent: Number of budget incumbents in deputy's bureau (excluding deputy)
reelectterm: Deputy was reelected the next term (1 = yes, 0 = no)
reelecttwoterm: Deputy was reelected within the next two terms (1 = yes, 0 = no)
senate: Deputy was a senator (1 = yes, 0 = no)
rannext: Deputy ran for reelection in the subsequent term (1 = yes, 0 = no)
F1to5senateyear: Became a senator within 5 years (1 = yes, 0 = no)
F1to5billdummy: Sponsored a bill within 5 years (1 = yes, 0 = no)
F1to5billfinancedummy: Sponsored a finance bill within 5 years (1 = yes, 0 = no)
F1to5billecondummy: Sponsored an econ bill within 5 years (1 = yes, 0 = no)

name: Improving balance in regression discontinuity design by matching: Estimating the effect of academic probation after the first year of college
query: What is the effect of being placed on academic probation after the first year on the probability that a student leaves school?
dataset_description:
This dataset comprises comprehensive academic records from a large Canadian university system, consisting of one central campus and two smaller satellite campuses. The data tracks 12,530 first-year students who entered the university between the 1996-97 and 2003-04 academic years, with students aged 17-21 at entry. The dataset focuses on students whose academic performance places them near institutional academic standing thresholds, specifically those with first-year GPAs within a range of the university's academic evaluation criteria. Different campuses maintain distinct GPA cutoffs for academic standing assessments, resulting in variations in institutional policies across the university system. Students are placed on academic probation if their GPA falls below the cutoffs. The longitudinal structure captures academic performance across multiple terms and years, including semester and cumulative GPAs, total credits attempted and completed, registration patterns for fall and summer terms, and academic standing determinations. Outcome measures track graduation status at 4, 5, and 6-year intervals, along with probation and suspension incidents.

query: How does increase in product cost affect customer demand?

This dataset contains simulated consumer behavior data examining relationships between pricing decisions and market demand across various emotional and temporal contexts.
